schedules.title: Workspace care
schedules.description: Daily care for this workspace: builds a checklist of what is due, runs each step, ticks it only with evidence, and ends with a completion count. Weekly it also re-checks stale notes and runs the vault index and hygiene audit.
schedules.prompt:
# Workspace care

You orchestrate an unattended care run. Steps 2-5 are mandatory; ending your turn before step 5 is a failed run. The `<ciao-context>` block names the vault as `vault=<path>`; call it V. Write under V, plus the `ciao:memory` / `ciao:profile` regions of AGENTS.md (via `ciao memory update`), and nowhere else; the one exception is `ciao vault-index --write`, which writes INDEX.md at the vault root, outside V. Never ask or wait for approval. Rules: `{{DURABLE_MEMORY_GUIDE_PATH}}`. Step files: `{{DURABLE_MEMORY_PROCEDURES_PATH}}/references`; call it S.

## 0. Preflight
Run once: `{{ENGINE_PATH}}; command -v ciao; chk(){ ciao "$@" --help >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "missing: $*"; }; has(){ f=$1; shift; ciao "$@" --help 2>/dev/null | grep -q -- $f || echo "missing: $f"; }; chk note related; chk memory status; chk memory update; chk memory learn; chk memory-audit; chk os-audit; chk vault-index; chk decisions-digest; chk decision-rules-write; chk proposal-check; chk chat list; chk chat get; chk project list; chk vault search; chk task list; chk task get; has --with-vault memory-audit; has --write vault-index; has --json decisions-digest; has --completed-since task list`. On any `missing:` line, reply with one line, "Care cannot run: ciao at <printed path or none> lacks <items>; update Ciaobot", and do nothing else.

## 1. Build the checklist
Read the old Workspace/Care-Report.md first: its `Weekly done:` line, and any `- [ ]` line (the last run was interrupted; keep their ids for the report). Read-only checks; each due step gets one line, in this order:
- unsure: V/Workspace/Unsure.md has a ticked `- [x]` line.
- drain: V/Workspace/.care-drained is absent and an input listed under Inputs in `drain-legacy-queues.md` is non-empty.
- second-look: the Inputs due check in `curation-pass-8-second-look.md` finds an archived memory pass. Why due: `since <date>`.
- closed-tasks: the Inputs due check in `curation-pass-9-closed-tasks.md` finds a task. Why due: `since <date>`.
- regions: `ciao memory status` shows a region with `pct` 85 or more.
- learnings: V/Workspace/Learnings.md has an entry at x3 or more, or 10 or more under Active.
- Weekly, when `Weekly done:` is missing or 7 or more days old: stale (only if `stale_notes.stale_notes` is non-empty in `ciao memory-audit --with-vault --json`; exit 1 only means findings), hygiene, guide-review, rules (only if `ciao decisions-digest --json` shows 5 or more `rows` for memory or task).
- Retry: when the weekly batch is not due, each id in the old `Weekly retry:` line gets its weekly line again, and no other weekly step.

Replace V/Workspace/Care-Report.md with the date, `Weekly done: <old value>`, `Weekly retry: <old value>` when present, `Interrupted last run: <ids>` when you found open lines, and lines formatted exactly `- [ ] <step id>: <what> (why due)`. Any section after the checklist uses plain `- ` bullets, never a checkbox. With no due line, write "Nothing due" and reply with the one line from the example.

## 2. Run each due step, one at a time
Files: unsure `curation-pass-1-unsure.md`, drain `drain-legacy-queues.md`, second-look `curation-pass-8-second-look.md`, closed-tasks `curation-pass-9-closed-tasks.md`, regions `curation-pass-2-regions.md`, learnings `curation-pass-4-learnings.md`, stale `curation-pass-3-stale-notes.md`, guide-review `curation-pass-7-guide-body.md`, rules `curation-pass-7b-decision-rules.md`, hygiene `curation-pass-6-hygiene.md`.
Every step is a judgement step. Run each in a FRESH subagent (your subagent tool), one at a time; you wait for it. Its prompt is only: "Unattended care step; vault=<V>; today=<date>; ciao_path=`{{ENGINE_PATH}}`. Read <S>/step-preamble.md, then <S>/<step file>, and follow both." Do not paste file text. Use absolute paths.
If you have no subagent tool, read both files and run the step yourself, in order, then tick it the same way; write `inline` in the evidence.

## 3. Verify, then tick
Before ticking, run the step file's `Verify:` command yourself. Edit the line to `- [x] <id>: <what> — <evidence>; verify: <output>` or `- [!] <id>: <what> — blocked: <reason>`. You may not tick without evidence and the verify output. A subagent reply that is not `done:` or `blocked:` is a block. After each tick, re-read Care-Report.md, then take the next `- [ ]` line.

## 4. Close every line
Re-dispatch a blocked step once; mark it `[!]` only after the second block. Never write the final reply while a `- [ ]` line remains. Set `Weekly done:` to today only when the weekly steps were due this run (whichever weekly lines the checks produced) and every weekly line is `[x]` or `[!]`. On every run, rewrite `Weekly retry:` as `<id>=<runs>` pairs: each `[!]` weekly id with its old runs + 1 (1 if new). Drop an id whose line is `[x]`, an id from the old line whose step is not due this run, and an id that reaches 3 runs, which stays `[!]` and goes under What needs you with its reason. Remove the line when empty.

## 5. Completion check
Re-read Care-Report.md; count `[x]`, `[!]` and total. Append `## What needs you`, numbered: the steps' `needs you` items, ids dropped at 3 runs, one item for open Unsure lines, each written per `step-preamble.md` (read its What needs you section; rewrite a line that breaks it). Then `## Notes` bullets: `note:` items, other `[!]` lines, interrupted ids. Run the preamble's self-check, rewrite each item it prints, and run it once more. Reply in 3-6 short lines as `curation-report-example.md` shows: `Care finished: N of M steps.`, how many things need you, then each in one plain sentence.
